caseno: Appeal from Appellate Decree Nos. 106 & 107 of 1965.
lawyer:
Md. Shamsul Huq Chowdhury ----- For the Appellant. 
No one ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Moulvi Ruhul Amin ----- Appellant.
Vs.
Bazal Huq and others ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
These two appeals arise out of judgment and decrees passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong dated 10.3.64 in other Appeal Nos. 311 and 312 of 1963 affirming those passed by the learned Mansif North Roasan Chittagong dated 3-7-63 in other Suit Nos. 123 and 124 of 1962 and arise out of two suits for redemption in both the appeals the plaintiff is the common and the respondents were different. Both were tried analogously by the Courts below and covered by the same judgment. Here also both the appeals will be covered by the same judgment. 

 5. The learned Subordinate Judge on appeal affirmed judgment and decree passed by the learned Munsif, also held that the documents Exts. B and B(1) were out and out sale with condition of repurchase and were not mortgage by conditional sale. As against the same the present second appeals have been preferred. Mr. Md. Shamsul Huq Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the plaintiff, appellant but the defendants have not appeared in spite of notice upon them. 

 6. Mr. Md. Shamsul Huq Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the appellant submits that the Courts below erred in law in holding that the documents Ext. B and B(1) were documents of out and out sale with condition of repurchase. He submits that on a reading of documents themselves it will transpire that by these documents the predecessor of the plaintiff mortgaged the suit land and the document: were not deeds of absolute sale with a condition of repurchase: that these were covered by section 58(c) and were mortgages by conditional sale. He further submits that the Courts below have misconstrued the documents Ext. B and B(1) and therefore judgments and decrees passed by the Courts below are not maintainable. Mr. Chowdhury, the learned Advocate has taken me through the documents and he has pointed out that though the documents showed that those were documents of ostensible sale but actually the details incorporated in the documents would tend to show that absolute right was not transferred and those were not documents of sale but mortgage by Conditional sale. Mr. Chowdhury, the learned Advocate, submits that though the documents Exts. B and B (1) stated that the mortgage shall have absolute right in the land transferred; the same was subject to following conditions; 

 and these conditions are the same in both Exts. B and B(1). This condition proves that the Kabala though ostensibly showed that those were sale deed but actually they were mortgage by conditional sale. The condition referred to above clearly shows that if money is not paid within the stipulated period of 15 years the purchaser shall have the right to force on these documents and convert the same into a document of purchase. The sentence, is to the effect that “দলিল বরবাদ সিদ্ধক্রমে আসল কবলা পরিণত করিয়া। বরবাদ সিদ্ধক্রমে means "by way of foreclosure" and this condition refers to section 67 of the Transfer of Property Act by which right of foreclosure is given to the mortgagee. Section 67 of the Transfer of Property Act is to the effect that "in the absence of a contract to the contrary, the mortgage has, at any time after the mortgage money has become due to him, and before a decree has been made for the redemption of the mortgaged property or the mortgage money has been paid or deposited as hereinafter provided, a right to obtain from the Court a decree that the mortgagor shall be absolutely debarred of his right to redeem the property, or a decree that the property be sold". Thus we find that the said contents in the documents Exts. B and B(1) are in consonance with the provisions of section 67 of the Transfer of Property Act. The mention of the term; “দলিল বরবাদ সিদ্ধক্রমে আসল কবলা পরিণত করিয়া” definitely speaks of a final Kabala by virtue of a suit for foreclosure. Though in the earlier part of the documents Exts. B and B(1) absolute right has been given to mortgagor those rights were subject to the latter portion which has been quoted above. As such this was nothing but an ostensible sale. It may be noted that in the said documents the mortgagors ostensibly sold the property on condition that on such repayment being made the sale shall become void. One of the terms in the document were to the effect that if the consideration money is paid back after 8 years of the execution of document, within 15 years the mortgagees shall return the documents as also the mortgaged property to the mortgagors. The conditions were also embodied the same document in terms of proviso to section 58(C), T.P. Act. The stipulation mentioned for return of the document with the mortgaged laid to the mortgagors together with the condition of foreclosure proves categorically that the said documents exts B and B(1) were mortgage by condition of repurchase. Thus, on a proper consideration of the deeds Exts B and B(1) I find that the Courts below tried in law construing those documents and as such they erred in holding that the said documents were out and out sale deeds, with condition to re-purchase. It may also be noted that the time that was given for redemption was a longer time i.e. 15 years and the price that was paid was loan. These are also circumstances which prove that the nature of the documents were not sale deed but mortgage. 

 The result, therefore, is that these appeals are allowed. The judgments and decrees passed by the Courts below are hereby set aside and the suits are deemed. There will be no order as to costs.
